Ridge Roll Rules

Roll four dice, pair them up and climb seven ridges. Roll on as long as you dare - if no pair fits, the climbing of the turn is lost. Whoever reaches the top of three ridges first wins.

The rules

The board
Seven ridges, each for the sums of two dice: 2 to 4 (11 steps), 5 (8 steps), 6 (10 steps), 7 (11 steps), 8 (10 steps), 9 (8 steps) and 10 to 12 (11 steps). Every ridge starts at the foot and ends at the top.
Your turn
Tap "Roll the dice": four dice are rolled. The buttons show the ways to make two pairs, with the two sums. Choose one: each sum moves your climber one step up its ridge. Then roll on, or stop and make camp.
Three climbers
In one turn you have at most three climbers. A ridge that already has a climber of this turn uses it again. If both sums of a pair fit, both are used; if only one fits, only that one; if each would fit but not both, you choose one of them.
Turn lost
If no sum of the roll fits - the ridges are full of climbers, closed or climbed to the top - the turn is lost: the climbing of this turn is gone. Your camps stay.
Making camp
If you stop, your climbers become camps: next time you start from there. A camp is your own black marker (circle, square, triangle or star); a climber of this turn is a white ring with a thick black edge.
The top
If you make camp at the top of a ridge, the ridge is yours: it is hatched and closed for everyone, and the other players' camps on it are removed.
Winning
Whoever claims three ridges first wins at once (before the game you can choose two). If every ridge is claimed and nobody has enough, the most ridges win; players level on that win together.
Who starts
Who starts is drawn by lot. In test games with computers the first player won clearly more often, so the lot keeps it fair.
The computer
Easy takes the pair with the most steps and stops after three good rolls. Medium and Hard prefer ridges they already climb and short ways to the top; Hard reckons the chance of losing the turn with the next roll.

Example

You roll 3, 4, 1 and 5. The pairs: 3 + 4 = 7 and 1 + 5 = 6, or 3 + 1 = 4 and 4 + 5 = 9, or 3 + 5 = 8 and 4 + 1 = 5. You choose 7 and 6: one step up the ridge of 7 and one up the ridge of 6. Now you have two climbers and may roll on.
